    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When the HTML parser processes an end tag named "script" in the text insertion mode, it must set the script element's script text slot to its child text content before preparing the script element.</description>
    <spec_quote>An end tag whose tag name is "script"
:   ...

    Set script’s [script text](#htmlscriptelement-script-text) value to its child text content.

    If the active speculative HTML parser is null, then prepare the script
    element script.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R137">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When a parser-inserted script element's content is modified mid-parse before the closing script tag is processed, the user agent must protect against treating the untrusted mutation as trusted script text.</description>
    <spec_quote>The above algorithm doesn’t account for the case when the script element’s content is changed mid-parse. Implementors must ensure they protect against this case.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R138">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When parsing SVG script elements, the user agent must apply equivalent parser slot-setting behavior to populate SVGScriptElement's script text slot.</description>
    <spec_quote>There’s no proper definition for the processing of SVG script elements. However, implementations must apply a similar change to the processing of `SVGScriptElement`s.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R139">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>During HTML's "prepare the script element" algorithm, the user agent must execute "Prepare the script text" on the script element and abort script preparation without executing the script if it throws an error.</description>
    <spec_quote>5. Execute the [Prepare the script text](#prepare-the-script-text) algorithm on el. If that algorithm threw an error, then return.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R140">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>During HTML's "prepare the script element" algorithm, the script's source text must be read from the element's script text slot rather than its child text content.</description>
    <spec_quote>6. Let source text be el’s
   ~~child text content.~~
   [script text](#htmlscriptelement-script-text) value.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R141">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When preparing an SVGScriptElement for execution, the user agent must apply equivalent script text verification and use its script text slot as source text.</description>
    <spec_quote>There’s no proper definition for the processing of SVG script elements. However, implementations must apply a similar change to the processing of `SVGScriptElement`s.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R142">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When preparing script text for an HTMLScriptElement or SVGScriptElement whose script text slot does not equal its child text content, the user agent must validate the child text content via "get Trusted Type compliant string" expecting TrustedScript in sink group 'script' using the script's Document's relevant global object and sink name "HTMLScriptElement text" or "SVGScriptElement text", updating script text or rethrowing any error.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. Let sink be "`HTMLScriptElement text`" if script is an `HTMLScriptElement`; otherwise "`SVGScriptElement text`".
2. If script’s [script text](#htmlscriptelement-script-text) value is not equal to its child text content,
   set script’s [script text](#htmlscriptelement-script-text) to the result of executing [get Trusted Type compliant string](#get-trusted-type-compliant-string), with the following arguments:

   * `TrustedScript` as expectedType,
   * script’s `Document`’s relevant global object as global,
   * script’s child text content attribute value as input,
   * sink,
   * `'script'` as sinkGroup.

   If the algorithm threw an error, rethrow the error.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R143">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When validating an element attribute value for Trusted Types, the user agent must evaluate enforcement against the element's node document's relevant global object in sink group 'script'.</description>
    <spec_quote>6. Return the result of executing [get trusted type compliant string](#get-trusted-type-compliant-string) with the following arguments:

   * expectedType
   * newValue as input
   * element’s node document’s relevant global object as global
   * sink
   * 'script' as sinkGroup</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R144">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>Event handler content attributes with a null attribute namespace on elements in the HTML, SVG, or MathML namespace must require TrustedScript with sink name "Element " followed by the attribute name.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. If attributeNs is null, « HTML namespace, SVG namespace, MathML namespace » contains element’s namespace, and attribute is the name of an event handler content attribute:

   1. Return (`Element`, null, attribute, `TrustedScript`, "Element " + attribute).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R145">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>The srcdoc attribute in the null namespace on an HTMLIFrameElement must require TrustedHTML with sink name "HTMLIFrameElement srcdoc".</description>
    <spec_quote>| `HTMLIFrameElement` | null | "srcdoc" | `TrustedHTML` | "HTMLIFrameElement srcdoc" |</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R146">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>The src attribute in the null namespace on an HTMLScriptElement must require TrustedScriptURL with sink name "HTMLScriptElement src".</description>
    <spec_quote>| `HTMLScriptElement` | null | "src" | `TrustedScriptURL` | "HTMLScriptElement src" |</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R147">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>The href attribute in the null namespace on an SVGScriptElement must require TrustedScriptURL with sink name "SVGScriptElement href".</description>
    <spec_quote>| `SVGScriptElement` | null | "href" | `TrustedScriptURL` | "SVGScriptElement href" |</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R148">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>The href attribute in the XLink namespace on an SVGScriptElement must require TrustedScriptURL with sink name "SVGScriptElement href".</description>
    <spec_quote>| `SVGScriptElement` | XLink namespace | "href" | `TrustedScriptURL` | "SVGScriptElement href" |</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R149">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>In the require-trusted-types-for CSP pre-navigation check, any navigation request whose URL scheme is not "javascript" must immediately return "Allowed".</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If request’s url’s scheme is not `"javascript"`, return `"Allowed"` and abort further steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R150">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>In the require-trusted-types-for CSP pre-navigation check for a "javascript" URL, the serialized URL with the leading "javascript:" stripped must be processed through the default policy expecting TrustedScript with the request's client's global object and sink "Location href", returning "Blocked" if an error is thrown or the result is not a TrustedScript.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. Let urlString be the result of running the URL serializer on request’s url.
3. Let encodedScriptSource be the result of removing the leading `"javascript:"` from urlString.
4. Let convertedScriptSource be the result of executing [Process value with a default policy](#process-value-with-a-default-policy) algorithm, with the following arguments:

   * `TrustedScript` as expectedType
   * request’s clients’s global object as global
   * encodedScriptSource as input
   * `"Location href"` as sink

   If that algorithm threw an error or convertedScriptSource is not a `TrustedScript` object, return "Blocked" and abort further steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R151">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>After the default policy returns a TrustedScript in the require-trusted-types-for CSP pre-navigation check, "javascript:" must be prepended to the stringified result and parsed with the URL parser, returning "Blocked" if URL parsing fails.</description>
    <spec_quote>5. Set urlString to be the result of prepending `"javascript:"` to stringified convertedScriptSource.
6. Let newURL be the result of running the URL parser on urlString. If the parser returns a failure, return `"Blocked"` and abort further steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R152">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>If URL parsing succeeds in the require-trusted-types-for CSP pre-navigation check, the navigation request's url must be replaced with the newly parsed URL and the check must return "Allowed".</description>
    <spec_quote>7. Set request’s url to newURL.

   Note: No other CSP directives operate on `javascript:` URLs in a pre-navigation check. Other directives that check javascript: URLs
   will operate on the modified URL later, in the inline check.
8. Return `"Allowed"`.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R153">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>Checking whether a sink type requires Trusted Types must inspect global's CSP list for a policy with a "require-trusted-types-for" directive matching the sink group, returning true if an enforcing policy matches and false if no matching policy is found.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. For each policy in global’s CSP list:

   1. If policy’s directive set does not contain a directive
      whose name is `"require-trusted-types-for"`, skip to the next policy.
   2. Let directive be the policy’s directive set’s directive whose name
      is `"require-trusted-types-for"`
   3. If directive’s value does not contain a [trusted-types-sink-group](#trusted-types-sink-group) which is a match
      for sinkGroup, skip to the next policy.
   4. Let enforced be true if policy’s disposition is `"enforce"`, and false otherwise.
   5. If enforced is true, return true.
   6. If includeReportOnlyPolicies is true, return true.
2. Return false.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R154">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When global's CSP list contains a report-only policy with a matching "require-trusted-types-for" directive, "Does sink type require trusted types?" must return true when includeReportOnlyPolicies is true.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. Let enforced be true if policy’s disposition is `"enforce"`, and false otherwise.
   5. If enforced is true, return true.
   6. If includeReportOnlyPolicies is true, return true.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R155">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When generating a sink type mismatch CSP violation for the "Function" sink, any leading "function anonymous", "async function anonymous", "function* anonymous", or "async function* anonymous" prefix must be stripped from the sample string.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. If sink is `"Function"`, then:

   1. If sample starts with `"function anonymous"`, strip that from sample.
   2. Otherwise if sample starts with `"async function anonymous"`, strip that from sample.
   3. Otherwise if sample starts with `"function* anonymous"`, strip that from sample.
   4. Otherwise if sample starts with `"async function* anonymous"`, strip that from sample.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R156">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>On a sink type mismatch, for every policy in global's CSP list containing a "require-trusted-types-for" directive matching the sink group, the user agent must create a CSP violation for "require-trusted-types-for" with resource set to "trusted-types-sink" and execute CSP's Report a violation on it.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. For each policy in global’s CSP list:

   1. If policy’s directive set does not contain a directive
      whose name is `"require-trusted-types-for"`, skip to the next policy.
   2. Let directive be the policy’s directive set’s directive whose name
      is `"require-trusted-types-for"`
   3. If directive’s value does not contain a [trusted-types-sink-group](#trusted-types-sink-group) which is a match
      for sinkGroup, skip to the next policy.
   4. Let violation be the result of executing
      Create a violation object for global, policy, and directive
      on global, policy and `"require-trusted-types-for"`
   5. Set violation’s resource to `"trusted-types-sink"`.
   6. Let trimmedSample be the substring of sample, containing its first 40 characters.
   7. Set violation’s sample to be the result of concatenating the list « sink, trimmedSample « using `"|"` as a separator.
   8. Execute Report a violation on violation.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R157">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>For a sink type mismatch CSP violation, the violation's sample must be set to the sink name concatenated with "|" and the first 40 characters of the sample string.</description>
    <spec_quote>6. Let trimmedSample be the substring of sample, containing its first 40 characters.
   7. Set violation’s sample to be the result of concatenating the list « sink, trimmedSample « using `"|"` as a separator.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R158">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>In "should sink type mismatch violation be blocked by content security policy?", the result must be "Blocked" if any matching policy in global's CSP list has disposition "enforce", and "Allowed" otherwise.</description>
    <spec_quote>9. If policy’s disposition is `"enforce"`, then set result to
      `"Blocked"`.
5. Return result.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R159">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When a sink type mismatch occurs during "get trusted type compliant string", if CSP returns "Allowed" (report-only mode), the original stringified input must be returned without throwing; otherwise a TypeError must be thrown.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. Let disposition be the result of executing [should sink type mismatch violation be blocked by content security policy?](#should-sink-type-mismatch-violation-be-blocked-by-content-security-policy) algorithm,
      passing global, sink, sinkGroup, and stringified input as source.
   2. If disposition is `“Allowed”`, return stringified input and abort further steps.

      Note: This step assures that the default policy rejection will be reported, but ignored in a report-only mode.
   3. Throw a TypeError and abort further steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R160">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>Creating a Trusted Type policy must consult CSP via "should Trusted Type policy creation be blocked by content security policy?" and throw a TypeError without creating the policy if it returns "Blocked".</description>
    <spec_quote>1. Let allowedByCSP be the result of executing [should Trusted Type policy creation be blocked by content security policy?](#should-trusted-type-policy-creation-be-blocked-by-content-security-policy) algorithm with global,
   policyName and factory’s [created policy names](#trustedtypepolicyfactory-created-policy-names) value.
2. If allowedByCSP is `"Blocked"`, throw a TypeError and abort further steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R161">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When checking policy creation against a CSP policy containing a "trusted-types" directive, a violation must be triggered if the directive's value contains only the 'none' keyword.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. If directive’s value only contains a [tt-keyword](#tt-keyword) which
      is a match for a value `'none'`, set createViolation to true.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R162">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When checking policy creation against a CSP policy containing a "trusted-types" directive, a violation must be triggered if createdPolicyNames already contains policyName and the directive's value does not contain 'allow-duplicates'.</description>
    <spec_quote>5. If createdPolicyNames contains policyName and directive’s value does not contain a [tt-keyword](#tt-keyword) which is a match
      for a value `'allow-duplicates'`, set createViolation to true.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R163">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When checking policy creation against a CSP policy containing a "trusted-types" directive, a violation must be triggered if the directive's value contains neither a policy name matching policyName nor the wildcard '*'.</description>
    <spec_quote>6. If directive’s value does not contain a [tt-policy-name](#tt-policy-name),
      which value is policyName, and directive’s value does not contain a [tt-wildcard](#tt-wildcard), set createViolation to true.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R164">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When a Trusted Type policy creation CSP violation is triggered, the user agent must create a CSP violation for "trusted-types" with resource set to "trusted-types-policy" and sample set to the first 40 characters of policyName, and execute CSP's Report a violation on it.</description>
    <spec_quote>8. Let violation be the result of executing
      Create a violation object for global, policy, and directive on global, policy and
      `"trusted-types"`
   9. Set violation’s resource to `"trusted-types-policy"`.
   10. Set violation’s sample to the substring of policyName, containing its first 40 characters.
   11. Execute Report a violation on violation.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R165">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>In "Should Trusted Type policy creation be blocked by content security policy?", policy creation must return "Blocked" if any CSP policy that triggered a violation has disposition "enforce", and "Allowed" otherwise.</description>
    <spec_quote>12. If policy’s disposition is `"enforce"`, then set result to
       `"Blocked"`.
3. Return result.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R166">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When extracting a sanitizer configuration from parser options, a SanitizerPresets value ("default") must resolve to the built-in safe default configuration, a Sanitizer instance must resolve to its configuration, and a SanitizerConfig dictionary must be used directly.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. If sanitizerInput is a `SanitizerPresets`:

   1. Assert: sanitizerInput is `"default"`.
   2. Set configuration to the built-in safe default configuration.
5. Otherwise, if sanitizerInput is a `Sanitizer`:

   1. Set configuration to sanitizerInput’s configuration.
6. Otherwise, if sanitizerInput is a `SanitizerConfig`:

   1. Set configuration to sanitizerInput.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R167">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When parser options include a non-null sanitizer, the user agent must create a new Sanitizer object in the target realm and configure it with the resolved configuration and true.</description>
    <spec_quote>8. Let sanitizer be a new `Sanitizer` in realm.
9. Configure sanitizer given configuration and true.
10. Return sanitizer.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R168">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When constructing the callback argument for createParserOptions, "runScripts" must default to false and, if a sanitizer was provided in the input dictionary, "sanitizer" must be set to the newly created Sanitizer instance.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. Let runScriptsInput be dictionary["runScripts"], with default false.
2. Let argument be the ordered map «[ "runScripts" → runScriptsInput ]».
3. Let sanitizerInput be the result of [getting a sanitizer](#get-a-sanitizer-from-dictionary) from realm and dictionary.
4. If sanitizerInput is not null, set argument["sanitizer"] to sanitizerInput.
5. Return argument.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R169">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>An author-supplied SetHTMLUnsafeOptions or ParseHTMLUnsafeOptions dictionary must be treated as needing vetting under Trusted Types enforcement if runScripts is true or if sanitizer is present and is not an empty SanitizerConfig.</description>
    <spec_quote>A `SetHTMLUnsafeOptions` or `ParseHTMLUnsafeOptions` options needs vetting if
options["runScripts"] exists and is true, or if options["sanitizer"] exists and is not an empty `SanitizerConfig`.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R170">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When parser options enforcement fails due to a missing or rejecting default policy, the user agent must report a sink type mismatch violation to CSP with an empty string as source, returning the original input if CSP returns "Allowed" (report-only) or throwing a TypeError if CSP returns "Blocked".</description>
    <spec_quote>1. Let disposition be the result of executing [should sink type mismatch violation be blocked by content security policy?](#should-sink-type-mismatch-violation-be-blocked-by-content-security-policy) algorithm,
         passing global, sink, `"script"`, and the empty string as source.
      2. If disposition is `“Allowed”`, return input.
      3. Throw a `TypeError`.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R171">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When getting Trusted Type compliant input for an "html" document, if "get trusted type compliant parser options" returns a TrustedHTMLParserOptions instance, the sink must return the stringified input and those compliant options without requiring TrustedHTML string conversion.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. If documentType is `"html"`:

   1. Set compliantOptions to the result of calling [get trusted type compliant parser options](#get-trusted-type-compliant-parser-options), passing global, options, false, sink, and optionsFromAuthor.

      Note: Sinks that construct options themselves, rather than taking them from the author, pass false for optionsFromAuthor.
      For example, `createContextualFragment()` sets `runScripts` to true.
   2. If compliantOptions is an instance of `TrustedHTMLParserOptions`, return (stringified input, compliantOptions).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R172">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When getting Trusted Type compliant input for an "xml" document, the user agent must skip parser options vetting and always validate the markup string via "get trusted type compliant string" expecting TrustedHTML.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. If documentType is `"html"`:

   1. Set compliantOptions to the result of calling [get trusted type compliant parser options](#get-trusted-type-compliant-parser-options), passing global, options, false, sink, and optionsFromAuthor.

      Note: Sinks that construct options themselves, rather than taking them from the author, pass false for optionsFromAuthor.
      For example, `createContextualFragment()` sets `runScripts` to true.
   2. If compliantOptions is an instance of `TrustedHTMLParserOptions`, return (stringified input, compliantOptions).
3. Let compliantHTML be the result of calling [get trusted type compliant string](#get-trusted-type-compliant-string), passing `TrustedHTML`, global, input, sink, and `"script"`.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
</requirements_list>
